The test image clearly shows:
- White fluffy/cottony mycelial growth on soybean stems
- Large black sclerotia (hard, irregular black bodies) embedded in/on the white mold
- Bleached white stem tissue
- Damage at the stem/node level near soil

This strongly points to **White Mold**. Let me confirm with reference images.

The evidence is clear:

**Test image features:**
- Prominent white fluffy/cottony mycelial growth on soybean stems
- Large black sclerotia (hard, irregular black bodies) embedded in the white mold at the nodes
- Bleached/pale white stem tissue
- Stem damage near soil line

**White Mold reference match:**
- Identical white fluffy mycelial growth on stems (bottom-left panel)
- Same stem-level damage pattern

**Ruled out:**
- Anthracnose: shows brown/tan dried stems with small scattered acervuli, no white growth
- Diaporthe: shows linear rows of small black pycnidia on dry stems, no white mycelium
- The large black sclerotia + white mycelium combination is pathognomonic for White Mold (*Sclerotinia sclerotiorum*)
